issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes every OTLP LoggingHandler from the root logger as a global side effect
issues.detail: The fix strips all instances of opentelemetry's LoggingHandler from the root logger before force_flush, mutating global logging state including handlers the caller installed independently. Scope the removal to the handler this module installed, or track it explicitly. Global mutation of the root logger to fix a local deadlock is bad taste and violates the function's documented contract.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP LoggingHandler by isinstance walk over root logger handlers
issues.detail: The replay path scans logging.getLogger().handlers and picks the first LoggingHandler match. Any prior OTLP handler from another subsystem eats the replay and the real one is skipped; if none exists it silently no-ops. Hold the handler reference created in _setup_cloud_tracer and replay into that. This also leaks telemetry internals through the JobContext boundary.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is unbounded with no size cap or drop policy
issues.detail: buffer is an unbounded list[LogRecord] retained from _on_setup until init_recording or _on_cleanup. If a job hangs before either while logging at volume, it grows without limit. Cap it (ring buffer or max bytes) and drop oldest with a warning on flush. A crash-log feature that OOMs the worker is worse than the bug it fixes.

issues.description: init_recording is overloaded as a cleanup/teardown path in _on_cleanup with synthetic RecordingOptions
issues.detail: _on_cleanup invokes init_recording with traces=False, logs=True to opportunistically flush crash logs, conflating setup and teardown responsibilities under one name. Its preconditions are now ambiguous when prior init failed or partial state exists. Split into init_recording and a dedicated _ensure_crash_log_pipeline / teardown call so the contract is visible.

issues.description: Patch bundles unrelated worker.py race fix and makefile/test changes with the crash-log feature
issues.detail: Reordering _pending_assignments before _queue_msg in worker.py is a real race fix; dropping -n auto and excluding test_plugin_google_stt.py from the makefile is test-infra. Neither is motivated by the PR title. Split into separate commits so bisect, revert, and review attribution work per module boundary.

issues.description: Bare except Exception around init_recording in _on_cleanup risks leaving telemetry half-initialized
issues.detail: The except clause catches Exception, logs, then calls _stop_log_buffering only in the failure path. If init_recording raises after partially setting up the OTLP pipeline, half-initialized telemetry leaks into shutdown. Narrow the catch, or ensure _stop_log_buffering runs unconditionally before propagating unexpected errors.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the core idea — buffer logs early, flush via OTLP when recording initializes, force-resolve shutdown on crash — is the right shape, but execution has consistent flaws. Three reviewers independently flag global root-logger mutation in _shutdown_telemetry, isinstance-walk handler discovery in _flush_early_log_buffer, and an unbounded buffer. The PR also overloads init_recording as a cleanup path and bundles unrelated worker.py race and makefile parallelism changes. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — scope handler ownership explicitly, bound the buffer, and split the patch.
